correctness.rationale: The inverse recovers the first two old coordinates from the new second and third and then divides the first-coordinate residual by δ. Substitution into H=x+(δ−σ)y+δz cancels the y,z terms in H∘F−H and leaves x²+(δ−σ−1)x+α=(x−c)²+ε. On an interval of N steps the increment is at least Nε. For ε>0 the height difference between two points in the cube is at most 2R(1+|δ−σ|+δ); separately H(F^Np)≥H(p)+Nε and H≤(1+|δ−σ|+δ)||·||∞ give the liminf bound and eventual permanent exit. At ε=0, bounded forward orbits have summable squared first-coordinate deviations by telescoping, hence all three coordinates converge by the shifts. For any full bounded orbit the same sum over all integers is finite; both limiting states are the fixed one, so both limiting heights agree and the sum is zero. This applies to any point of F(K)=K by invertibility, not to arbitrary forward-invariant compact sets. Integrating the identity under a compactly supported invariant law gives the moment equation, and the marginal shifts prove Dirac uniqueness at equality. Solving the fixed-point equation gives the stated two fixed points below the fold. This is an exact existence boundary, not a claim that the runtime bound is the optimal finite exit time, or that all trajectories converge at the fold.
